questions.question: Which of the following national parks emerged as one of the two top-performing protected areas in India, earning a Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) score of 92.97%, in the assessment conducted by the Wildlife Institute of India in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dachigam National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the assessment conducted by the **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)** released in **June 2025**, **Dachigam National Park** achieved an exceptional **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE)** score of **92.97%**.
 
• This score places it as one of the **top two performing protected areas** in the country, reflecting outstanding administrative and ecological management.
 
• The **MEE process** is a globally recognized tool used to evaluate the management of **National Parks** and **Wildlife Sanctuaries**, focusing on **design**, **appropriateness**, and **delivery of conservation objectives**.
 
• The evaluation highlights the park's success in **habitat restoration**, **wildlife protection**, and **community engagement** programs within the **Jammu and Kashmir** region.
 
• The high performance in the **2025 cycle** underscores the efficiency of the **Department of Wildlife Protection** in maintaining the fragile **Himalayan ecosystem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dachigam National Park**:
 
 
• Located in the **Zabarwan Range** of the **Himalayas**, approximately **22 kilometers** from **Srinagar**.
 
• It was established in **1910** as a protected area and was later declared a **National Park** in **1981**.
 
• The name **Dachigam** signifies **"Ten Villages,"** referring to the relocation of ten villages to establish the park.
 
• It is the primary habitat of the **Hangul** (also known as the **Kashmiri Stag**), which is **Critically Endangered** and the **State Animal** of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
 
 
• **Other Protected Areas Mentioned**:
 
 
• **Ranthambore National Park**: Located in **Rajasthan**, it is one of the most prominent **Tiger Reserves** in **India**, known for its significant **Bengal Tiger** population.
 
• **Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP)**: Located in **Himachal Pradesh**, it was established in **1984** and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** recognized for its **high-altitude biodiversity**.
 
• **Nanda Devi National Park**: Situated in **Uttarakhand**, it is part of the **Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks** **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and surrounds the peak of **Nanda Devi**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)**: An autonomous institution under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, established in **1982** and headquartered in **Dehradun**.
 
• **MEE Parameters**: The evaluation uses a framework of **30 indicators** across six elements: **context**, **planning**, **inputs**, **process**, **outputs**, and **outcomes**.
 
• **Conservation Success**: The **92.97%** score is a testament to the rigorous **anti-poaching** measures and **scientific monitoring** techniques implemented to protect the **alpine** and **sub-alpine** forests.
 
• **Flora and Fauna**: Apart from the **Hangul**, the park hosts **Himalayan Black Bear**, **Leopards**, and rare birds like the **Monal Pheasant** and **Crimson Tragopan**.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, which of the following cities hosted the 5th edition of Lok Samvardhan Parv organised by the Ministry of Minority Affairs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kochi, Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **5th edition** of the **Lok Samvardhan Parv** was organized by the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**, Government of India, in **2025**.
 
• The event was hosted in the city of **Kochi, Kerala**, specifically held at the iconic **Marine Drive Ground** from **February 14 to February 23, 2025**.
 
• This initiative is designed to provide a national platform for **artisans**, **craftsmen**, and **culinary experts** belonging to minority communities to showcase and sell their traditional indigenous products.
 
• The **5th edition** in **Kochi** emphasized the theme of **“Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”** (Development along with Heritage), focusing on the preservation of India's rich cultural diversity while promoting economic growth.
 
• The fair featured over **300 artisans** from more than **30 States and Union Territories**, displaying a wide array of **handicrafts**, **handlooms**, and **traditional heritage products**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Minority Affairs:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** was carved out of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and created on **January 29, 2006**.
 
• It acts as the nodal agency for the overall policy, planning, coordination, evaluation, and review of the regulatory and development programs for **minority communities** including **Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains**.
 
• As of **2025**, the ministry is led by the **Union Minister Kiren Rijiju**, who has emphasized the socio-economic empowerment of these communities through skill development.
 
 
 
• **PM VIKAS Scheme:**
 
 
• The **Lok Samvardhan Parv** is an integral part of the **Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS)** scheme.
 
• **PM VIKAS** is a central sector scheme that aims to improve the livelihoods of **artisans** and **minority communities** through **skill development**, **education**, and **entrepreneurship**.
 
• It converges five erstwhile schemes of the Ministry: **Seekho aur Kamao**, **USTTAD**, **Hamari Dharohar**, **Nai Roshni**, and **Nai Manzil**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact and Digital Integration:**
 
 
• The event significantly contributes to the **employment generation** of traditional craftsmen, providing them with direct access to urban markets without the interference of middlemen.
 
• To further enhance reach, many products displayed at **Lok Samvardhan Parv** are integrated with the **GeM (Government e-Marketplace)** portal, allowing artisans to sell their products to government departments and global audiences digitally.
 
• The fair also features **“Bawarchikhana,”** a dedicated section for traditional **Indian cuisines**, which promotes the culinary heritage of different regions of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Host City Significance:** **Kochi**, known as the **“Queen of the Arabian Sea,”** was chosen to highlight the **cultural confluence** of **South India** and to provide a gateway for artisans to tap into the thriving tourism and trade market of **Kerala**.
 
• **Vocal for Local:** The event is a practical implementation of the **Hon'ble Prime Minister's** vision of **‘Vocal for Local’** and **‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’** (Self-reliant India).
 
• **Cultural Programs:** Apart from commerce, the **Lok Samvardhan Parv** in **Kochi** featured daily **cultural performances** by renowned artists, showcasing **Ghazals**, **folk dances**, and **classical music**, thereby fostering a spirit of **‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following revolutionary books was authored by Veer Savarkar in 1923, whose birth anniversary was commemorated on 28th May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindutva: Who is a Hindu?**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **Hindutva: Who is a Hindu?** was authored by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** (popularly known as **Veer Savarkar**) and was published in **1923**.
 
• The book was written while **Savarkar** was imprisoned in **Ratnagiri** jail and under internment; it was initially published under the pseudonym **'A Maratha'** to avoid British censorship.
 
• In this work, **Savarkar** systematically defined the concept of **Hindutva** as an all-encompassing political and cultural identity, distinct from the religious rituals of **Hinduism**.
 
• **Savarkar's** birth anniversary falls on **28th May**; the year **2025** commemorates his **142nd birth anniversary**, as he was born in **1883** in the village of **Bhagur**, **Nashik** district, **Maharashtra**.
 
• The core thesis of the book posits that a **Hindu** is anyone who considers **India** (Bharatvarsha) as their **Pitribhu** (Fatherland) and **Punyabhu** (Holy land). ***Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **My Experiments with Truth:**
 
 
• This is the autobiography of **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi** (Mahatma Gandhi).
 
• It was originally written in **Gujarati** and published as a series in his journal **Navjivan** between **1925** and **1929**.
 
• The book covers **Gandhi's** life from his childhood in **Porbandar** to the year **1921**, focusing on his spiritual and moral development.
 
 
 
• **The Discovery of India:**
 
 
• Written by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first **Prime Minister** of India.
 
• It was written during his imprisonment at **Ahmednagar Fort** between **1942** and **1945** following the **Quit India Movement**.
 
• The book provides a comprehensive analysis of Indian history, philosophy, and culture from the **Indus Valley Civilization** to the British **Raj**.
 
 
 
• **India Wins Freedom:**
 
 
• This is an autobiographical account by **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**, a senior leader of the **Indian National Congress** and India's first **Education Minister**.
 
• The book offers an insider's view of the **Indian Independence** movement, the **Partition of India**, and **Azad's** personal views on the political leaders of that era.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Revolutionary Contributions:** **Veer Savarkar** founded the secret society **Abhinav Bharat Society** in **1904** to promote armed rebellion against British rule.
 
• **1857 War of Independence:** He authored another famous book, **The Indian War of Independence 1857**, in which he was among the first to describe the **1857** uprising as the **"First War of Independence"** rather than a mere sepoy mutiny.
 
• **Cellular Jail:** For his revolutionary activities, he was sentenced to two life terms (50 years) and sent to the **Cellular Jail** (Kala Pani) in the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** in **1911**.
 
• **Political Leadership:** He served as the **President** of the **Hindu Mahasabha** from **1937** to **1943**, where he advocated for the rights of the Hindu community and a militarized **India**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following initiatives supports athletes’ training for Olympics and Paralympics as of 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Target Olympic Podium Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** was launched in **September 2014** by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS)**. Its primary objective is to identify and provide support to India’s elite athletes to help them achieve podium finishes at the **Olympic Games** and **Paralympic Games**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The scheme was significantly revamped in **April 2018** to establish a more robust technical support team and provide holistic assistance to athletes, including customized training programs and international exposure.
 
• It provides a monthly **Out-of-Pocket Allowance (OPA)** of **Rs. 50,000** to athletes in the **Core Group** and **Rs. 25,000** to those in the **Development Group** to cover daily incidental expenses.
 
• As of **2025**, the scheme continues to be the flagship initiative for high-performance sports in India, focusing on upcoming major events like the **2028 Los Angeles Olympics**.
 
• The **Mission Olympic Cell (MOC)** is a dedicated body under this scheme that evaluates athlete performance and approves financial assistance for training, equipment, and travel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Come and Play Scheme**: 
 
 
• This initiative was launched by the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** in **2011**.
 
• Its main focus is on **grassroots development** and encouraging the general public and youth to utilize the various sports facilities available at **SAI centers** across the **country**.
 
• It is not specifically designed for elite-level **Olympic** or **Paralympic** podium training. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Go and Play Scheme**:
 
 
• There is no official government-recognized initiative named the "Go and Play Scheme" for Olympic training; it is often used as a distractor for the "Come and Play Scheme." ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **National Sports Fund (National Sports Development Fund - NSDF)**:
 
 
• The **NSDF** was established in **1998** under the **Charitable Endowments Act, 1890**.
 
• Its purpose is to mobilize resources from **government**, **non-government**, and **private sectors** for the promotion of sports in India.
 
• While the **NSDF** provides the financial backing for various programs including **TOPS**, it is a funding mechanism rather than the specific training initiative for elite athletes. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mission Olympic Cell (MOC)**: A specialized committee chaired by the **Director General of SAI** that meets frequently to clear proposals for **foreign training**, procurement of **high-end equipment**, and hiring of **personal coaches** or **physiotherapists**.
 
• **Khelo India Programme**: Launched in **2018**, this program works alongside **TOPS** to identify talent at a **young age** and provide a scholarship of **Rs. 5 lakh** per annum for eight years to talented players.
 
• **Elite Athlete Support**: Under **TOPS**, the government bears the entire cost of **international competitions**, **sports science support**, and **medical insurance** for the selected athletes.
 
• **Focus Areas**: The scheme prioritizes sports where India has a high potential for medals, such as **Wrestling**, **Boxing**, **Shooting**, **Archery**, **Badminton**, and **Athletics**.

questions.question: As of May 2025, what is the maximum FDI allowed through the Automatic Route in India's defense sector for companies seeking new industrial licenses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**74%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **May 2025**, the Government of India permits Foreign Direct Investment (**FDI**) in the defense sector up to **74%** through the **Automatic Route** for companies seeking new industrial licenses.
 
• This significant policy shift was formalized through **Press Note 4 (2020 Series)** issued by the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)** in **September 2020**, aimed at boosting local manufacturing.
 
• For investments exceeding **74%**, the **Government Route** is applicable, allowing up to **100%** FDI where it is likely to result in access to modern technology or for other reasons to be recorded by the government.
 
• The policy stipulates that any foreign investment in the defense sector is subject to **Security Clearance** by the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and as per the guidelines of the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• The liberalization of FDI limits is a core component of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan** (Self-Reliant India Mission), designed to encourage **Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs)** to set up production facilities within **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of FDI in Defense:**
 
 
• In **2001**, the defense sector was first opened to private participation with an FDI cap of **26%**.
 
• The limit was increased to **49%** under the **Automatic Route** in **2014** to stimulate the **Make in India** initiative.
 
• The current **74%** limit serves to provide foreign investors with management control, thereby incentivizing the transfer of high-end technology to **Indian** subsidiaries.
 
 
 
• **Automatic vs. Government Route:**
 
 
• The **Automatic Route** signifies that the foreign investor or the Indian company does not require any prior approval from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** or the **Government of India** for the investment.
 
• The **Government Route** (or Approval Route) requires prior clearance from the concerned administrative ministry, which in this case is the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• Defense manufacturing is primarily regulated under the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951** and the **Arms Act, 1959**.
 
• All foreign investments are subject to **National Security** clauses, allowing the government to review any investment that may affect the sovereignty and integrity of the nation.
 
 
 
• **Sectoral Impact:**
 
 
• The increase to **74%** has facilitated major global firms like **Safran**, **Lockheed Martin**, and **Boeing** to explore deeper collaborations with **Indian** partners.
 
• It aims to reduce the **Defense Import Bill**, as **India** has historically been one of the world's largest importers of major arms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fresh Industrial Licenses:** The **74%** automatic limit is specifically applicable to companies seeking **New Industrial Licenses**. Existing licensees seeking to infuse fresh foreign investment up to **49%** must follow specific declaration protocols.
 
• **Review Authority:** The **Department of Defence Production (DDP)** functions as the nodal agency for processing cases under the **Government Route** and monitors the **Indigenization** progress.
 
• **Equity Cap:** While the **74%** route is automatic, the government maintains the right to scrutinize any investment on the grounds of **Security**, ensuring that the control of critical defense infrastructure remains transparent.
</ul

questions.question: Where was the second phase of the Khelo India Winter Games, 2025, held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulmarg, Jammu and Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **second phase** of the **Khelo India Winter Games 2025** was officially held in the world-famous ski resort of **Gulmarg**, located in the **Baramulla district** of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• This phase of the multi-sport event took place in **February 2025**, following the successful completion of the first phase held earlier in the year.
 
• The competition in **Gulmarg** featured high-intensity winter sports disciplines, including **Alpine Skiing**, **Snowboarding**, **Nordic Skiing**, and **Ski Mountaineering**, attracting top athletes from across the country.
 
• The **Jammu and Kashmir Sports Council**, in collaboration with the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, spearheaded the organization to promote winter tourism and professional sports in the region.
 
• The games serve as a platform to identify talent for representing **India** in international arenas like the **Asian Winter Games** and the **Winter Olympics**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Gulmarg, Jammu and Kashmir**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phase 1 of KIWG 2025**:
 
 
• The **first phase** of the **2025** edition was conducted in **Leh**, **Ladakh**.
 
• It primarily focused on ice-based sports such as **Ice Hockey**, **Figure Skating**, and **Speed Skating**.
 
 
 
• **Mascot of the Games**:
 
 
• The official mascot for the **Khelo India Winter Games 2025** is **'Sheen-e-She'** (or **Shan**), which is a **Snow Leopard**.
 
• This mascot symbolizes the **biodiversity** of the **Himalayas** and the resilience required for winter sports.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure and Location**:
 
 
• **Gulmarg** is situated at an altitude of approximately **2,650 meters** and is home to the **Gulmarg Gondola**, one of the highest cable cars in the world.
 
• The region provides ideal conditions for **winter sports** due to its heavy snowfall and naturally groomed slopes like the **Kongdoori** and **Apharwat** peaks.
 
 
 
• **Participating Entities**:
 
 
• Athletes representing various **States**, **Union Territories**, and organizations like the **Indian Army** (**HAWS - High Altitude Warfare School**) and **ITBP** participate in these games.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Growth of Winter Sports**: Since the inaugural edition in **2020**, the **Khelo India Winter Games** have significantly increased the popularity of niche sports like **Curling** and **Ice Skating** in **India**.
 
• **Economic Impact**: Hosting these games helps boost the **economy** of **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh** by promoting **sports tourism** during the peak winter months.
 
• **Youth Engagement**: Under the **Khelo India** initiative, the government provides financial assistance and world-class coaching to selected athletes through **Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCE)**.
 
• **Historical Context**: **Gulmarg** has hosted the majority of the **KIWG** editions (including **2020**, **2021**, **2023**, and **2024**), establishing itself as the **winter sports capital** of **India**.
</ul

questions.question: ‘Agnibaan - SOrTeD’ (Sub-Orbital Technology Demonstrator) was launched on 30 May 2024 from India's first private launch pad called ______, established by Agnikul.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhanush**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Agnibaan - SOrTeD** (**Sub-Orbital Technological Demonstrator**) mission was successfully launched on **30 May 2024**.
 
• It was launched from **Dhanush**, which is **India's first private launchpad**, established by the space startup **Agnikul Cosmos**.
 
• The **Dhanush** launchpad is located within the premises of the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** (**SDSC SHAR**) in **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• This mission marked a significant milestone as it was the **first-ever launch** from a private launchpad in **India** and featured the world's first **single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine**, named **Agnilet**.
 
• The flight was a **sub-orbital mission**, designed to test the flight systems and the **3D-printed engine** technology before full-scale orbital launches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agnikul Cosmos**:
 
 
• It is an **IIT Madras**-incubated space startup founded in **2017** by **Srinath Ravichandran** and **Moin SPM**.
 
• The company focuses on developing **cost-effective** and **customizable** launch vehicles for small satellites.
 
• In **2022**, **Agnikul** inaugurated **India's first private launchpad** and mission control center at **Sriharikota**.
 
 
 
• **Agnilet Engine**:
 
 
• The **Agnilet** is a **semi-cryogenic engine** that uses **Liquid Oxygen** (**LOX**) and **Kerosene** as propellants.
 
• It is unique because it is **entirely 3D-printed** as a **single piece** of hardware, significantly reducing the number of components and assembly time.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework**:
 
 
• The launch was supported by **IN-SPACe** (**Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre**) and **ISRO** (**Indian Space Research Organisation**).
 
• **IN-SPACe** acts as a single-window nodal agency to promote and authorize **private sector participation** in the **Indian space sector**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for the Indian Space Sector**:
 
 
• Following the success of **Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S** in **November 2022**, the **Agnibaan** mission further cements **India’s** position in the global **private space industry**.
 
• The use of **additive manufacturing** (**3D printing**) in rocket engines showcases **India's** technological advancements in **deep-tech** sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Agnibaan** rocket is a **customizable**, **two-stage** launch vehicle capable of carrying a payload of up to **100 kg** to a **Low Earth Orbit** (**LEO**) of about **700 km**.
 
• The **SOrTeD** mission specifically utilized a **single-stage** version of the rocket to demonstrate **vertical ascent** and **controlled flight**.
 
• The establishment of **private launchpads** like **Dhanush** is part of the **Indian Space Policy 2023**, which encourages **Non-Government Entities** (**NGEs**) to own and operate space infrastructure.

questions.question: What was the agriculture growth rate forecast for India in FY 2025 as per the Economic Survey 2024–25, released in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024-25**, tabled in **Parliament** in **January 2025**, projected the growth rate for the **Agriculture and Allied Sectors** to be **3.8%** for the financial year **FY 2025**.
 
• This forecast indicates a significant recovery and expansion compared to the previous financial year, **FY 2024**, where the growth rate was estimated at a lower **1.4%** due to erratic weather patterns. ***Hence, the correct answer is 3.8%.***
 
• The survey attributes this optimistic growth projection to the expectation of a **normal monsoon** and favorable **reservoir levels** across the country, which are critical for the **Kharif** and **Rabi** sowing seasons.
 
• The agriculture sector remains a vital pillar of the Indian economy, contributing approximately **18-19%** to the **Gross Value Added (GVA)** and providing a livelihood for nearly **45%** of the population.
 
• The improvement in agricultural output is expected to boost **rural demand**, which in turn supports the broader recovery of the **Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG)** and **automobile** sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overall GDP Growth Forecast**: 
 
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024-25** has projected **India’s real GDP growth** to be in the range of **6.5% to 7%** for **FY 2025**.
 
• This growth trajectory maintains India's position as the fastest-growing major economy in the world, supported by strong **domestic investment** and **private consumption**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Economic Survey**: 
 
 
• The **Economic Survey** is a flagship document prepared by the **Department of Economic Affairs** under the **Ministry of Finance**.
 
• It is authored by the **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)** of India, a position currently held by **Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran**.
 
• The document provides a detailed report card of the economy for the closing financial year and offers insights and outlooks for the upcoming year.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Food Inflation**: 
 
 
• The survey highlighted that while **headline inflation** is moderating, **food inflation** remains a key area of concern for policymakers.
 
• Supply-side measures and the expected **3.8%** growth in agriculture are seen as essential tools to stabilize the prices of essential commodities like **cereals** and **vegetables**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Structural Reforms in Agriculture**: 
 
 
• The **2024-25** survey emphasizes the need for **digitalization** in the farming sector through the **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)** for agriculture.
 
• It highlights the success of the **PM-KISAN** scheme, which provides direct income support to **11 crore** farmers, ensuring financial stability.
 
 
 
• **Credit Growth**: 
 
 
• The **Institutional Credit** to the agriculture sector has seen a steady rise, with the government setting high targets for **Agricultural Credit** to ensure farmers have access to affordable loans.
 
 
 
• **Capital Expenditure (CapEx)**: 
 
 
• A major theme of the **January 2025** release is the continuation of high **Capital Expenditure** by the government, which includes building **irrigation facilities**, **cold chains**, and **rural roads** to support the **3.8%** growth target.

questions.question: Which veteran Indian actor-director, known as 'Bharat Kumar' for his patriotic films, passed away on 4 April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manoj Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manoj Kumar** is a legendary **Indian** actor, director, and screenwriter who became an iconic figure in **Bollywood** during the **1960s** and **1970s**.
 
• He earned the popular moniker "**Bharat Kumar**" due to his penchant for acting in and directing films with strong **patriotic** themes, where his character was often named **Bharat**.
 
• The veteran actor-director passed away on **4 April 2025** (as per the provided data), marking the end of a cinematic era dedicated to **nationalism** and **Indian** values.
 
• His significant contribution to cinema was recognized by the **Government of India** with the **Dadasaheb Phalke Award** in **2015**, which is the highest honor in **Indian** cinema.
 
• He is best remembered for his "patriotic trilogy" of films: **Shaheed** (**1965**), **Upkar** (**1967**), and **Purab Aur Paschim** (**1970**).
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Manoj Kumar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early Life and Background**:
 
 
• Born as **Harikishan Giri Goswami** on **July 24, 1937**, in **Abbottabad** (then part of **British India**, now in **Pakistan**).
 
• His family migrated to **Delhi** during the **Partition of India** in **1947**.
 
• He adopted the screen name **Manoj Kumar** after being inspired by **Dilip Kumar's** character in the **1949** film **Shabnam**.
 
 
 
• **Directorial Milestones**:
 
 
• His directorial debut, **Upkar** (**1967**), was produced at the request of Prime Minister **Lal Bahadur Shastri** to promote the slogan "**Jai Jawan Jai Kisan**" following the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1965**.
 
• In **1974**, he directed **Roti Kapada Aur Makaan**, a massive hit that addressed social issues like unemployment and poverty in **India**.
 
• His **1981** film **Kranti** was another major success that focused on the **Indian Independence Movement**.
 
 
 
• **Awards and Honors**:
 
 
• He received the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in the year **1992**.
 
• Over his career, he won multiple **Filmfare Awards**, including **Best Actor** for **Be-Imaan** (**1972**) and **Best Director** for **Upkar**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Analysis of Other Options**:
 
 
• **Amitabh Bachchan**: Known as the "**Angry Young Man**" and "**Shahenshah**," he was born in **1942** and remains active in the film industry. While he has played patriotic roles, he is not referred to as "**Bharat Kumar**."
 
• **Dilip Kumar**: Often called the "**Tragedy King**," he was one of the greatest actors in **Indian** history. He passed away on **July 7, 2021**, at the **age** of **98**.
 
• **Rajesh Khanna**: Recognized as the first "**Superstar**" of **Indian** cinema, he was famous for his romantic roles and massive fan following in the late **1960s** and early **1970s**. He passed away on **July 18, 2012**.
 
 
 
• **Cinematic Style**:
 
 
• **Manoj Kumar's** films were unique for blending **entertainment** with **socio-political** messages, often contrasting **Western** materialism with **Indian** spiritualism and culture.
 
• His portrayal of **Bhagat Singh** in **Shaheed** remains one of the most authentic depictions of the freedom fighter in **Indian** film **history**.
 
 
</ul
